fact: La Tribune du Faso, from the digital transition ministry's communications office, reports that on 25 June 2025 the two ministers reviewed work on the national pupil file, online enrolment and school identity cards, with a roadmap still awaited and progressive enrolment of pupils due to start at the next school year; no school is said to be using it.
The article states that the national platform is meant to follow pupils from primary school to university, and that enrolment had not begun at 25 June 2025.

The article states that the national pupil file is being built by the technical teams of the ministry of digital transition and the ministry of basic education, whose ministers reviewed it on 25 June 2025.
The article states that the design and implementation of the national pupil platform has the technical and financial support of the WURI project; it names no domestic budget line.

The World Bank appraisal document of 14 April 2025 states that the project will support the design and deployment of a centralised digital platform for student management and monitoring, with a smartphone application for data collection at school level and a web interface for the central administration; it is still to be designed and no school is said to use it.
The appraisal document describes the student management platform as a future deployment under a project for pre-primary and primary education, and reports it in use at no level at 14 April 2025.

The appraisal document calls the planned platform a key step towards complete digitisation of student records, and states that key education data and information are currently stored mainly as hard copies; no date is given, so the document's date is used.

The appraisal document names the Ministry of Basic Education (MEBAPLN) as implementing agency of the project that will build the student management platform, which is to be the student management module of the Education Management Information System.

The appraisal document places the student management platform under Component 3 of the project (US$42.7 million: US$17.7 million IDA and US$25.0 million GPE), within a US$203.1 million operation financed by IDA and the GPE fund; it names no domestic budget line for the platform.
